findings.finding: Kaiser's own FY2026 guide (adjusted EBITDA +45-55% on FY2025's $310M = $450-480M) less H1 2026's booked $295M ($129M Q1 + $166M Q2) implies H2 EBITDA of only $155-185M, i.e. $78-93M a quarter and about flat on H2 2025's ~$168M (Q3'25 ~$80M incl. a 12-week Trentwood outage, Q4'25 $88M), while Q2 ex-metal-lag EBITDA was ~$139M and conversion revenue is guided to the top of +10-15%; a Q3 near the Q1 ex-lag run-rate (~$93M) or above forces a raise of the FY range, which is the line this stock has paid for (Q2: beat and raise, +9.9%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-22): record quarter, FY EBITDA guide raised to +45-55%, stock +9.91%. Q1 2026 (2026-04-22): record quarter and raised outlook, +1.11%. Q3 2025: big beat (adj EPS $1.86 vs ~$0.89), +19.54%. Q4 2025 (no numeric guide): -8.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a raise, the stock would not sit 22% below its 52-week high with a 20d run-up of -2.3%, and the published consensus ($2.08-2.17 EPS) would not sit in the guide-implied band; management explicitly built the guide on neutral metal lag and normalized scrap spreads, which the sell-side models mechanically.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 results ($129M EBITDA, $36M lag) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000811596/000119312526170615/kalu-ex99_1.htm and FY2025 release ($310M) https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260218643721/en/Kaiser-Aluminum-Corporation-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results; all company documents, so this is one arithmetic on company numbers. Partly shares the metal-price premise with finding 2. Counter: the CFO said H2 carries heavier maintenance and fewer shipping days (finding 5), which is part of why the guide is low.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 metal prices rose through the quarter relative to the cost basis Kaiser carried out of Q2: the CFO said exiting Q2 its weighted-average metal inventory cost matched the forward Midwest Transaction Price of $2.45/lb, while LME cash went from ~$3,073/t on 1 July to ~$3,250-3,325/t in September and the Midwest premium held ~$1.10-1.11/lb (Fastmarkets 110-112c on 7 July, Platts 109.7c on 10 Sept), putting the Midwest Transaction Price near $2.50/lb in July and ~$2.57/lb in September; that points to neutral-to-favourable Q3 metal lag against a guide and consensus built on neutral, partly offset by Alcoa's average realized price falling 4.7% q/q (lower average pass-through, mostly a net-sales effect).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Metal lag drove the last two beats: Q1 2026 ~$36M favourable lag (+1.11%), Q2 2026 ~$27M (+9.91%); FY2025 ~$93M of favourable lag.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of ~$2.1-2.2 is consistent with zero lag; Kaiser does not disclose lag until the print and sell-side models tend to assume the company's neutral guidance, so a positive lag line would show up as an EPS beat. If priced, consensus would have drifted up through September and the stock would not have fallen 22% off its high.

findings.finding: Crown Holdings reported on 2026-10-19 that North American beverage can shipments rose 6% in Q3 2026 (vs +5% in Q2 and a 3-4% full-year regional guide), and that October shipments were stronger, a direct-customer-class read for Kaiser's Warrick can-sheet volumes (packaging is ~half of Kaiser's pounds; Q2 packaging shipments +10.4%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Packaging mix was cited as a driver of both 2026 beats (Q1 +1.11%, Q2 +9.91%); no isolated packaging surprise in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: Crown spoke two days before Kaiser and after any sell-side preview; it is an industry read, and Kaiser's CEO already said packaging would not keep improving in H2, so most of it is inside the guide - hence small.
findings.independence: Trade-press summary of the same Crown call: https://www.packagingdive.com/news/beverage-packaging-aluminum-cans-earnings-beer/803547/ (same event). findings.finding: Aluminium prices turned down into Q4: LME cash fell from ~$3,248/t at end-September to $3,102/t by 7 October (~-4.5%), the Midwest premium had already eased from a $1.19/lb June record to $1.097/lb by 10 September on Canada tariff talk, and the H1 2026 LME high was ~$3,850; a falling Midwest Transaction Price produces unfavourable metal lag and narrower scrap spreads for Kaiser, so the Q4 commentary on the call (22 Oct) risks a cautious tone or a range that keeps H2 low even after a Q3 beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 print (Feb 2026), qualitative outlook amid metal tailwinds fading: -8.85%. In June 2026 the CEO noted metal fell 'roughly $0.30 a pound very quickly'.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is 22% off its high and the sell-side already assumes neutral lag. What would be unpriced is management quantifying a negative Q4 lag; if priced, the stock would not have rallied +3% over the last five sessions into the print.
